title: Simplify the proposed bootstrap after applying its own Branch Rule

spec.unmetRequirement: The original bootstrap was structurally consistent but had not justified seven independently discoverable skills, a centralized authoritative ledger, mirrored relationships or additional change/learning registries. The repository must earn its own complexity, not turn its implementation choices into requirements.
spec.simplestViableOption: One primary agent, one governing skill with selectively loaded references, canonical typed artifacts with stable IDs and single-owner links, a read-only derived graph validator, focused tests and minimal CI. Use normal Git/review controls for learning and approvals.
spec.selectedOption: Adopt that minimum. Keep one flat engineering directory with one JSON artifact per stable ID and no manifest or aggregate ledger. Keep the six expertise topics as reference documents, not independent skills. Derive all reverse links and transitive views at validation time. Maintain evidence conventions and a human-reviewed A-F behavioral rubric, without a hosted model runner.
spec.capabilityGained: The same outcome-first procedure and inspectable traceability with fewer discovery boundaries and reconciliation obligations. Individual artifacts support focused diffs; deterministic file discovery and in-memory graph derivation need no registry, graph service or additional persistent state.
alternatives: Seven independent skills: rejected at bootstrap. The original adr-procedure proposal treated requested expertise areas as independent packaging requirements and omitted one skill plus selective references. No independent reuse, invocation or context-isolation evidence earned the six extra discovery surfaces. Extraction may be reconsidered after demonstrated reuse or context failures.

Centralized JSON ledger: rejected as the authoritative layout for this bootstrap. The original adr-contract proposal justified machine-readable state over prose, not centralized storage over individual typed artifacts. A single file can be adequate for small repositories, but is not necessary for graph integrity and creates broader editing contention. Separate artifacts add deterministic discovery and cross-file validation, which the existing validator can perform.

Mirrored and repeated transitive links: rejected regardless of storage layout. Capability verification lists duplicated evaluation capability lists; implementation decision lists repeated capability decisions. These required reconciliation without adding evidence. Store each semantic edge once and derive inverse/transitive navigation.
README-only or prompt-only enforcement: insufficient for machine validation. Retain concise instructions, discoverable procedure, JSON Schema validation and deterministic relationship checks.

Separate change/learning registries and mandatory registration of every incidental file: not earned. Git diffs, human review and consequential decision artifacts can preserve correction history. Bind significant implementation paths, report other unbound files, and do not claim textual learning status proves actual codification.

Multiple engineering agents, runtime agents, MCP, cloud/application/deployment architecture, hooks and autonomous production modification: intentionally deferred until a named workload requirement earns them. Tool count and expertise count do not determine agent count.
spec.simplerOptionAssessment: One skill with references is sufficient for selective expertise loading. Canonical individual files are sufficient for authoritative state; no second ledger or committed graph is needed. The minimal validator, built-in Node tests and one CI workflow remain earned by repeatable structural gates. Ajv and YAML remain small locked tooling dependencies for standard parsing, not workload technology choices. One A-F run per scenario is an initial discovery check, not a statistical reliability claim; the previous arbitrary three-run gate is not retained as a new registry or acceptance burden.
spec.operationalResponsibility: Maintain schemas, stable IDs, single-owner relationship semantics, reference discoverability, implementation bindings, Node 24 tooling, locked parser dependencies and pinned CI actions. Review graph/validator changes for weakened controls. Humans authenticate approvals, judge reasoning/evidence, run behavioral scenarios and configure repository review protections.
spec.rationale: First Golden Path evolution, 2026-09-22: observe the proposed scaffold; evaluate its branches against the mission; learn that topic count does not justify skill count and machine-readable state does not require a central ledger; hypothesize that one skill plus references and derived traceability are sufficient; propose simplification; receive explicit human approval; implement and prove structural behavior; retain behavioral acceptance as pending. The original proposals were never approved, so their rejected reasoning is preserved here rather than retaining obsolete implementation or marking them as formerly approved decisions. Structural validation before the review passed 35 records, demonstrating internal consistency, not necessity. This decision codifies the reasoning; actual implementation correctness is established by tests and review, not by this paragraph. Approval covers repository architecture and scoped local implementation only. Existing local WRITE and ephemeral test/CI WRITE effects remain bounded; no production authority is added.

approval.reviewer: Human repository owner requesting this change in the Copilot conversation
approval.source: Copilot conversation 6c416aca-ddec-4c4b-a47c-861b5ea52bc4; user response to the bootstrap self-review on 2026-09-22. The statement and adopted scope are preserved here; no hosted review URL or authenticated reviewer identity is asserted.
approval.statement: Approved. Proceed with the minimum viable bootstrap architecture you recommended.
approval.scope: One primary agent; one governing golden-path skill with references; canonical individual artifacts and single-owner relationships; derived views; no authoritative ledger; deterministic validation/tests/minimal CI; explicit approval states; behavioral/evidence conventions. Treat this review as the first architecture evolution. No runtime or production architecture is authorized.
